notes:
### Overview: South Dakota Net Corporate Income Tax
South Dakota does **not** impose a general corporate income tax, unitary business income tax, or personal income tax on multistate business corporations. The state does, however, levy a Bank Franchise Tax on financial institutions under South Dakota Codified Laws (SDCL) Chapter 10-43 based on net income. 

* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no changes between years).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/business-tax/
  * https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/sales-use-tax/sales-and-use-tax-guide/

---

### 1. Apportionment Formula
* **General Multistate Business Income:** Not applicable / no general corporate income tax is imposed.
* **Financial Institutions (Bank Franchise Tax):** An equally weighted three-factor apportionment formula is used. Net income is apportioned to the state by multiplying net income by a fraction, the numerator of which is the property factor plus the payroll factor plus the receipts factor, and the denominator of which is 3.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-22.1

---

### 2. Sourcing of Services and Intangibles (Market-Based Sourcing vs. Cost of Performance)
* **General Multistate Businesses:** Not applicable / no general corporate income tax.
* **Financial Institutions (Bank Franchise Tax):**
  * **Receipts from Services:** Sourced using a **cost/place of performance** standard. Receipts from fees, commissions, service charges, and other receipts from rendering financial or fiduciary services are included in the South Dakota numerator if the service is "principally performed in South Dakota" (SDCL 10-43-25.3). Exception: "Affiliated service income" is sourced under SDCL 10-43-25.8 based on the location of the borrower/collateral/credit card customer (market location).
  * **Receipts from Intangibles / Securities:** Sourced based on principal place of business or location of deposits/borrowers:
    * Interest, dividends, and net gains from transactions in securities are sourced to South Dakota if the institution's principal place of business is in South Dakota (SDCL 10-43-25.5).
    * Receipts from securities used to maintain reserves against deposits are sourced based on the ratio of South Dakota deposits to total deposits everywhere (SDCL 10-43-25.6).
    * Interest, fees, penalties, and net gain from loans are sourced based on the real property location (if real property secured) or the borrower's billing address (if not real property secured) (SDCL 10-43-25.2).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
  * Services: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-25.3
  * Affiliated Services: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-25.8
  * Securities: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-25.5
  * Securities Reserves: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-25.6
  * Loan Receipts: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-25.2

---

### 3. Special Industry Apportionment Formulas
* **General Multistate Businesses:** Not applicable / no corporate income tax is imposed on other industries (transportation, broadcasting, telecommunications, etc.).
* **Financial Institutions:** South Dakota Codified Laws Chapter 10-43 provides a dedicated industry apportionment scheme solely for financial institutions (banks, savings and loan associations, and production credit associations), defining property, payroll, and receipts specifically for financial assets and activities (SDCL 10-43-22.1 through SDCL 10-43-25.9).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43

---

### 4. Form or Schedule Used to Compute Apportionment
* **General Corporate Multistate Businesses:** Not applicable (no general corporate return or apportionment form exists).
* **Financial Institutions:** Apportionment is reported and calculated as part of the **Bank Franchise Tax Return** filed electronically via the Department of Revenue’s online portal (EPath). Taxpayers must attach work papers calculating the apportionment factors (receipts, property, and payroll factors) to the return.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/bank-franchise-tax/
  * https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/bank-franchise-tax/guidance-on-foreign-dividend-recapture/
  * https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/64:26:02:04

### 1. Income or Franchise Tax Nexus (including Economic Nexus / Bright-Line Thresholds)

* **General Corporate Income Tax / Corporate Franchise Tax:**
  * South Dakota does not impose a general corporate income tax or a general corporate franchise tax. 
  * Consequently, there are no economic nexus standards or bright-line factor-presence dollar/transaction thresholds for general corporate income or franchise tax purposes.
  * **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
  * **Source:** 
    * South Dakota Department of Revenue, Business Tax: https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/business-tax/

* **Bank Franchise Tax (Financial Institutions Only):**
  * South Dakota imposes a Bank Franchise Tax exclusively on financial institutions (SDCL Chapter 10-43).
  * **Nexus Standard:** Imposed on each financial institution "doing business in this state or licensed to do business in this state during any part of its tax year" (SDCL § 10-43-2), or "regularly engaged in business in South Dakota at any time during the year". There are no bright-line factor-presence or economic nexus dollar/transaction thresholds established by statute or regulation.
  * **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
  * **Sources:**
    * South Dakota Department of Revenue, Bank Franchise Tax: https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/bank-franchise-tax/
    * South Dakota Legislature, SDCL § 10-43-2: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-2

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold & Measurement Period

* **Sales Threshold Amount:** Gross sales / gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, products transferred electronically, or services delivered into South Dakota exceeding **$100,000**.
* **Transaction Count:** **None** (0 transactions). The former alternative threshold of 200 or more separate transactions was repealed effective July 1, 2023 (SL 2023, ch 38, § 1) and does not apply.
* **Measurement Period:** The **previous or current calendar year**.
* **Registration Timeline:** Under SDCL § 10-64-2.1, remote sellers meeting the threshold are required to register and begin remitting by the first day of the first month that begins at least 30 days after meeting the threshold.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Sources:**
  * South Dakota Legislature, SDCL § 10-64-2: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-64-2
  * South Dakota Legislature, SDCL § 10-64-2.1: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-64-2.1
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue, Sales & Use Tax: https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/sales-use-tax/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue, Remote Seller Bulletin (August 2025): https://dor.sd.gov/media/wjhbsuuv/remote-seller-bulletin.pdf

---

### 3. State's Stated Position on P.L. 86-272 Protection

* **Position:** **not found**
  * *Context:* South Dakota does not impose a corporate or personal net income tax; therefore, neither the South Dakota Department of Revenue nor the South Dakota Legislature publishes guidance, rules, or determinations interpreting or applying Public Law 86-272 (15 U.S.C. § 381).

notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax
* **Status / Rates:** South Dakota does not impose a personal/individual income tax.
* **Tax Years:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (no change).
* **Official Sources:** 
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Taxes): https://dor.sd.gov/individuals/taxes/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Sales and Use Tax Guide): https://dor.sd.gov/media/w3jdvh11/sales-and-use-tax-guide.pdf

---

### 2. Corporate Income or Franchise Tax
* **Corporate Income Tax:** South Dakota does not impose a general corporate income tax.
* **Bank Franchise Tax (Financial Institutions):** Imposed on financial institutions doing business in the state based on net income assignable to South Dakota (SDCL § 10-43-4):
  * **6%** on net income of $400,000,000 or less
  * **5%** on net income exceeding $400,000,000 up to $425,000,000
  * **4%** on net income exceeding $425,000,000 up to $450,000,000
  * **3%** on net income exceeding $450,000,000 up to $475,000,000
  * **2%** on net income exceeding $475,000,000 up to $500,000,000
  * **1%** on net income exceeding $500,000,000 up to $600,000,000
  * **0.5%** on net income exceeding $600,000,000 up to $1,200,000,000
  * **0.25%** on net income exceeding $1,200,000,000
  * **Minimum Tax:** $200 per return ("In no case may the tax be less than two hundred dollars").
* **Tax Years:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (no change).
* **Official Sources:**
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Business Tax): https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Bank Franchise Tax): https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/bank-franchise-tax/
  * South Dakota Legislature (SDCL § 10-43-4): https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/10-43-4

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax Rate & Local Rates
* **State Rate:** **4.2%** on sales and use (reduced from 4.5% effective July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2027, under SDCL § 10-45-2 and Session Law HB 1137).
* **Local Option Rates:** Yes; municipalities are authorized to impose a local option sales and use tax (SDCL Chapter 10-52). The rate is generally **1% to 2%**. Both state and municipal taxes are reported on the same return.
* **Tax Years:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (no change; the 4.2% rate sunsets June 30, 2027).
* **Official Sources:**
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Sales & Use Tax): https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/sales-use-tax/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Municipal Tax): https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/municipal-tax/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue (Rate Reduction Announcement): https://dor.sd.gov/newsroom/department-of-revenue-updates-tax-system-for-decrease-in-state-tax-rate/

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes
* **Contractor's Excise Tax:** Imposed at **2%** on the gross receipts of prime contractors engaged in construction services or realty improvement projects in South Dakota (SDCL Chapters 10-46A and 10-46B). (A bid factor of 2.041% may be used when preparing a customer bid/bill to recover the tax). Applies to 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official Source:* https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/contractors-excise-tax/
* **Municipal Gross Receipts Tax (MGRT):** Municipalities may impose a **1%** gross receipts tax in addition to general municipal sales tax on alcoholic beverages, eating establishments, lodging accommodations, and admissions to amusement/athletic/cultural events (SDCL Chapter 10-52A). Applies to 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official Source:* https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/municipal-tax/
* **Tourism Tax:** Imposed at **1.5%** on the gross receipts of lodging/hotels, campgrounds, motor vehicle rentals, recreational equipment rentals/services, spectator events, visitor attractions, and visitor-intensive businesses (SDCL Chapter 10-45D). Applies to 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official Source:* https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/tourism-tax/
* **Telecommunications Tax:** **4%** tax reported under the City & Special Jurisdiction return section. Applies to 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official Source:* https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/municipal-tax/

notes:
### South Dakota Income Tax Overview
South Dakota does not impose a personal income tax, a general corporate income tax, or a unitary income tax. As a result, standard individual, corporate, and pass-through entity income tax return requirements do not exist in the state. 

---

### 1. Individual Return Due Dates and Extensions (Calendar-Year Filers)
* **Fact:** South Dakota does not impose a personal/individual income tax; therefore, there are no individual income tax returns, filing due dates, or extension rules.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no change).
* **Official URL:** 
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue – General Public Tax Information: https://dor.sd.gov/individuals/taxes/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue – Sales and Use Tax Guide: https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/sales-use-tax/guidelines-bulletins/sales-and-use-tax-guide/

---

### 2. Corporate and Pass-Through Return Due Dates and Extensions
* **Fact:** 
  * **General Corporations & Pass-Through Entities:** South Dakota does not levy a corporate income tax or a pass-through entity income tax. There are no return due dates or extension provisions for general business entities.
  * **Financial Institutions Exception (Bank Franchise Tax):** Financial institutions doing business in the state are subject to the Bank Franchise Tax (SDCL Chapter 10-43).
    * **Due Date:** Each taxpayer must file the franchise tax return within 15 days after their federal income tax return is due.
    * **Extensions:** Requests to file an extension are due on or before the return's original due date. To qualify, the taxpayer must submit via email to `bankfranchise@state.sd.us`: (1) a cover letter requesting an extension, (2) a copy of the federal extension form, and (3) payment of the estimated tax by the original due date (minimum tax is $200 per return).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no change).
* **Official URL:** 
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue – Bank Franchise Tax: https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/bank-franchise-tax/
  * South Dakota Codified Law Chapter 10-43: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/Codified_Laws/2042732

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)
* **Fact:** Not found / Does not exist. South Dakota does not impose a personal or corporate income tax, and has enacted no pass-through entity tax legislation.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://dor.sd.gov/individuals/taxes/
  * https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/Codified_Laws

---

### 4. Composite or Group Nonresident Returns for Pass-Through Entities
* **Fact:** Not found / Does not exist. Because South Dakota does not levy income taxes on individuals or entities, composite or group nonresident returns do not exist.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://dor.sd.gov/individuals/taxes/

---

### 5. Estimated Tax Payments and Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Through Entities
* **Fact:** 
  * **Pass-Through Entities:** Not found / Does not exist. South Dakota has no income tax withholding or estimated tax payment requirements for pass-through entities or their nonresident owners.
  * **Bank Franchise Tax Note:** Under SDCL 10-43-30, financial institutions whose tax liability in the previous year exceeded $10,000 must make quarterly estimated payments (due the 15th day of January, April, July, and October for calendar-year filers).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** 
  * South Dakota Codified Law § 10-43-30: https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/Codified_Laws/2042732
  * https://dor.sd.gov/individuals/taxes/

---

### 6. Main Individual, Corporate, and Pass-Through Return Forms
* **Fact:** 
  * **Individual, General Corporate, and Pass-Through:** Not found / None exist, as South Dakota has no state income tax return forms.
  * **Bank Franchise Tax:** Financial institutions file the Bank Franchise Tax return electronically through the Department of Revenue’s online Filing and Payment portal.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** 
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue – Individual Forms / Resources: https://dor.sd.gov/individuals/
  * South Dakota Department of Revenue – Bank Franchise Tax: https://dor.sd.gov/businesses/taxes/bank-franchise-tax/
